decisions.label: Second Primary Malignant Neoplasm
decisions.description: A primary malignant neoplasm in a patient who has been already diagnosed with a primary malignant neoplasm in another anatomic site.

verification.note: NCIT:C95606 Second Primary Malignant Neoplasm; 'Additional Primary' means a second or subsequent primary tumor — distinct from a recurrence or metastasis. The NCIT term captures this concept. Label differs (Additional Primary vs Second Primary Malignant Neoplasm) but is the correct concept.

decisions.label: Premalignant Condition
decisions.description: A pathological process that precedes and often leads to the development of cancer.

verification.note: NCIT:C36032 Premalignant Condition; atypia and hyperplasia are abnormal cell growth states that precede malignancy. The NCIT premalignant condition class is a reasonable umbrella, though not an exact label match.

decisions.label: Recurrent Disease
decisions.description: The return of a disease after a period of remission.

verification.note: NCIT:C38155 Recurrent Disease; 'Local recurrence' is a specific form of recurrent disease occurring at or near the original site. NCIT:C38155 is the generic recurrence concept — the most appropriate available term.

decisions.label: Metastatic Neoplasm
decisions.description: A tumor that has spread from its original site of growth to another anatomic site.

verification.note: NCIT:C3261 Metastatic Neoplasm; 'Metastatic' as a specimen composition type refers to tumor material from a metastatic site. The NCIT term describes the neoplasm concept, not a specimen composition qualifier per se, but is the best available match.

decisions.label: Normal Tissue Sample
decisions.description: Tissue sample with cellular composition and architectural patterns expected for the particular anatomic site in which it belongs; no evidence of abnormal cellular infiltrates or tumor mass formation.

verification.note: NCIT:C162623 Normal Tissue Sample; correct concept for a normal (non-tumor) specimen. Label adds 'Tissue Sample' qualifier but the sense matches.

decisions.label: Tumor-Adjacent Normal Specimen
decisions.description: A specimen comprised of morphologically normal tissue collected from the area immediately surrounding a tumor in an experimental subject.

verification.note: NCIT:C164032 Tumor-Adjacent Normal Specimen; exact concept for normal tissue adjacent to a tumor.

decisions.label: Tissue Sample
decisions.description: A piece of tissue removed from an organism for examination, analysis, or propagation.

verification.note: NCIT:C19697 Tissue Sample; 'Tissue' as a specimen composition term means a tissue specimen (as opposed to cell line, blood, etc.). The NCIT term adds 'Sample' qualifier. Best available generic tissue specimen class.

decisions.label: Not Otherwise Specified
decisions.description: Not more specifically or particularly described than the stated category.

verification.note: NCIT:C19594 Not Otherwise Specified; standard NCIT qualifier for NOS.

decisions.label: Not Applicable
decisions.description: Determination of a value is not relevant in the current context.

verification.note: NCIT:C48660 Not Applicable; standard NCIT qualifier.

decisions.label: Not Reported
decisions.description: An indication that the required information was not provided.

verification.note: NCIT:C43234 Not Reported; standard NCIT qualifier.

decisions.label: Premalignant Condition
decisions.description: A pathological process that precedes and often leads to the development of cancer.

verification.note: NCIT:C36032 Premalignant Condition; label adds 'Condition' but the concept matches — tissue from a premalignant state.

decisions.label: Carcinoma In Situ
decisions.description: A neoplasm in which the malignant cells are confined to the epithelium of origin, without invasion of the basement membrane.

verification.note: NCIT:C2917 Carcinoma In Situ; 'Premalignant - in situ' refers to in situ lesions (confined to site of origin without invasion). The NCIT term is carcinoma-specific (not covering all premalignant in situ conditions) but is the most appropriate available concept.

decisions.label: Primary Neoplasm
decisions.description: A tumor at the original site at which it arose.

verification.note: NCIT:C8509 Primary Neoplasm; 'Primary' as a specimen composition type means the specimen is from the original primary tumor site. The NCIT term describes the neoplasm concept, not a composition qualifier, but is the best match.

decisions.label: Recurrent Disease
decisions.description: The return of a disease after a period of remission.

verification.note: NCIT:C38155 Recurrent Disease; 'Recurrent' as specimen composition means tissue from a disease recurrence. Best available NCIT match.

decisions.label: Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample
decisions.description: A specimen derived from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic.

verification.note: NCIT:C156444 Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample; the term says 'adjuvant' while the NCIT label says 'neoadjuvant' — both refer to specimens collected after therapy, but adjuvant therapy is given post-surgery while neoadjuvant is pre-surgery. Best available post-therapy specimen class.

decisions.label: Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample
decisions.description: A specimen derived from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic.

verification.note: NCIT:C156444 Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample; exact concept for a tumor specimen collected after neoadjuvant therapy.

decisions.label: Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample
decisions.description: A specimen derived from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic.

verification.note: NCIT:C156444 Post Neoadjuvant Therapy Sample; 'Tumor post-therapy' is the most generic form (any therapy). The NCIT term is neoadjuvant-specific. Best available post-therapy specimen class.

decisions.label: Unknown
decisions.description: Not known, observed, recorded, or reported as unknown by the data contributor.

decisions.label: Cell Line-Derived Xenograft
decisions.description: A transplantation of cancer cells derived from an established cancer cell line into an immunodeficient mouse.

verification.note: NCIT:C156443 Cell Line-Derived Xenograft; 'Xenograft' is a broader term for any foreign tissue transplant, while NCIT:C156443 is specifically cell line-derived xenograft. Best available NCIT match for xenograft specimens.
